c169.title: Building a Podcast Website
c169.story: Anna wanted a website for her podcast, so she called Max for help. First, Max bought a [[domain]] with the podcast's name. Then he paid for [[hosting]] on a fast [[web server]]. "I love [[web design]]," he said, "and your old logo needs a [[redesign]] too." He spent two evenings on the [[back end]], and Anna tested the simple [[interface]]. Max checked every [[pixel]] of the new logo in his [[web browser]]. "Why is the video page so slow?" Anna asked. Max explained that [[rendering]] big videos takes time on a small laptop. He also showed her how good [[post-processing]] makes her photos bright and clean. Finally, he added a [[real-time]] chat for her listeners. On Friday, the first fan wrote, "Great new site!"

c170.title: A Visit to a Data Center
c170.story: On Monday, Max's team visited a big [[data center]] outside the city. A friendly [[admin]] named Oleh met them at the door. He showed them long rows of machines, and every [[server]] had blinking lights. In the corner stood an old [[mainframe]] that still worked. "We keep popular pages in the [[cache]], so they open fast," Oleh said. "And our [[firewall]] stops strange connections every minute." He showed how each [[batch]] of data travels with the [[Internet Protocol]]. "That's why cloud [[computing]] is so cheap for small companies," he added. On the roof, Max saw a tall radio [[transmitter]]. Back at the office, he played his favorite online game. Thanks to the new connection, his [[ping]] was lower than ever.

c171.title: Anna Learns Data Science
c171.story: This fall, Anna started an online [[data science]] course. In the first lesson, she learned how an [[algorithm]] suggests songs to listeners. It finds each [[cluster]] of people with similar taste. "This is [[big data]]," the teacher said, "millions of songs and listeners." For homework, Anna got a small [[dataset]] about coffee shops in Kyiv. She changed one [[parameter]] and watched the results change. In the formula 3x, the [[coefficient]] was three, so the line went up fast. Then she drew a [[vector]] as an arrow on the graph. She colored the background with a soft blue [[gradient]]. Anna noticed a funny [[parallel]] between coffee orders and music taste. When she got bored, she drew a little [[spiral]] in the margin. The best café sat in the upper right [[quadrant]], with cheap coffee and great music.

c172.title: A Physics Lesson
c172.story: After the long summer, Taras felt his brain was in [[stasis]]. But his new physics teacher woke everyone up. "Everything around you is made of [[atoms|atom]]," she said. She drew a tiny [[electron]] flying around a [[proton]] and a [[neutron]]. "Light is made of [[photons|photon]], and a [[quark]] is even smaller than a proton," she added. Then she put a ringing phone in a glass jar and pumped out the air. In the [[vacuum]], nobody could hear the phone. "Lightning is a kind of [[plasma]]," she said, pointing at the storm outside. She explained that each nerve sends an electric [[impulse]] to the brain. Then she sang one high note, and a glass on her desk began to shake. "That's [[resonance]]," she laughed. At the end, she gave everyone a [[magnet]], and Taras couldn't wait for more.

c173.title: The Lemon Battery Project
c173.story: On Saturday, Max helped Taras with his science project about electricity. First, they read the label on a lamp: sixty [[watts|watt]]. A small battery gave one and a half [[volts|volt]]. "Always check the [[voltage]] before you plug something in," Max said. They measured a resistor, and it had one hundred [[ohms|ohm]]. Taras laughed at a unit called the [[henry]], because it sounded like a person's name. "It's an [[SI]] unit, just like the meter," Max explained. Then they built a lemon battery and pushed an [[electrode]] into each lemon. Max said that each [[ion]] carries a tiny charge through the juice. One electrode was a [[nickel]] coin, and the other was a [[zinc]] nail. Taras read that real phone batteries use [[cobalt]], not lemons. Finally, they read about a nuclear [[reactor]], but Taras still loved their tiny lemon light.

c174.title: In the Chemistry Lab
c174.story: Anna's friend Olya worked in a chemistry lab and invited Anna for a tour. First, Olya showed her a tank of [[hydrogen]]. A yellow powder of [[sulfur]] smelled like rotten eggs, and Anna made a face. Above the door, a sign glowed with red [[neon]] light. "Rust is iron [[oxide]]," Olya said, "and table salt is sodium [[chloride]]." She read a shampoo label to Anna: "Free of [[sulfates|sulfate]]." Then she explained that carbon has more than one [[isotope]]. "Plastic is a [[polymer]], and we make new ones here," she said proudly. When Anna cut her finger on a box, Olya cleaned it with [[peroxide]]. "Long ago, doctors used [[ether]] to put patients to sleep," she added. Anna's pencil broke, and Olya joked that its [[graphite]] needed a rest. The best part was a shiny [[chrome]] machine that studied a real [[meteorite]].

c175.title: Chemistry at Home
c175.story: On a rainy Sunday, Anna decided to read the labels on things at home. Mom's baking molds were made of [[silicone]], and the cleaning gloves were [[latex]]. The plant fertilizer had [[nitrate]] and [[phosphate]] for strong roots. Her hand gel was mostly [[ethanol]]. In the garage, Dad showed her the antifreeze with [[ethylene glycol]]. "Never use an [[aerosol]] spray near a fire," he warned. In the kitchen, Anna read that carrots are rich in [[beta-carotene]]. Her old paint box said that every color comes from a [[pigment]]. The water bottle listed each [[mineral]], like calcium and magnesium. Dad pointed to the small alarm on the wall that warns about carbon [[monoxide]]. Anna laughed, "The only poison here is the [[cyanide]] in my detective books!"

c176.title: A Night at the Observatory
c176.story: On Friday night, Anna and Max visited the city observatory. Through a big [[telescope]], Max saw a bright [[object]] near the moon. "Is it a UFO?" he whispered. "No, it's a small [[asteroid]]," the guide laughed. A minute later, a [[meteor]] crossed the sky, and Anna made a wish. Then a retired [[astronaut]] talked about the beauty of the [[cosmos]]. She explained what scientists think about the [[genesis]] of the universe. She showed a photo of a [[lander]] on Mars next to a deep [[crater]]. "Every second, billions of [[neutrinos|neutrino]] from the sun pass through your body," she said. The guide pointed straight up at the [[zenith]], the highest point of the sky. When Anna asked about the [[zodiac]], the guide smiled. "That's not science, but the stars are still beautiful."

c177.title: Anna's Psychology Experiment
c177.story: For her psychology class, Anna ran an [[experiment]]: does music help people study? Noise was one [[factor]], and sleep was another. Honesty was an important [[element]], so she explained every step. Test scores were her main [[indicator]] of success. Max kept losing [[focus]], and his low score hurt his [[ego]] a little. "We can't know that music helps [[a priori]]; we have to test it," Anna said. Half the group got "smart candy" and felt smarter, but it was just the [[placebo effect]]. "What a [[paradox]]: the candy did nothing, but it worked!" Max laughed. In her report, Anna wrote that being "smart" is partly a social [[construct]]. Feelings about the music formed a [[continuum]], from love to hate. Her professor praised her healthy [[skepticism]] and gave her an A.

c178.title: Genes and Germs
c178.story: Anna's aunt Lida works at a [[biotech]] lab near the university. One day, she invited Anna to visit. "Here we study the human [[genome]]," she said. She showed a photo of a sheep and said it was a [[clone]]. Under the [[microscope]], Anna saw a [[mutant]] fly with tiny extra wings. Then Lida showed her a [[microbe]] that makes a dangerous [[toxin]]. "This [[enzyme]] breaks the toxin down, and this [[inhibitor]] stops the microbe from growing," she explained. Next, Anna looked at muscle cells and learned that the protein [[actin]] helps them move. "Our team also helps doctors fight [[Ebola]] and [[anthrax]]," Lida said. At home, Anna told Max, "Maybe I'll become a scientist too!"

c179.title: Brain, Mood and Hormones
c179.story: On Tuesday, Anna went with her friend Ira to an open lecture at medical school. The professor showed a picture of a [[neuron]], one of billions in the brain. "This outer layer is the [[cortex]]," she said. She explained how each [[receptor]] catches chemicals like [[serotonin]], which affects mood. "An [[antidepressant]] can help when a person feels sad for a long time," she said. Then she talked about [[mania]], when people barely sleep, and [[paranoia]], when they trust no one. A student asked about [[amnesia]], when a person loses memories. The professor said that [[autism]] is simply a different way a brain develops and works. Hormones matter too, like [[testosterone]] and [[estrogen]]. At the end, she tapped Ira's knee, and her leg jumped: a perfect [[reflex]]!

c180.title: A Week at Medical School
c180.story: Anna's friend Ira told her about a busy week at medical school. On Monday, her anatomy group studied a [[cadaver]] with great respect. The teacher held up a [[scalpel]] and explained each step. They looked inside the [[abdomen]] and found the small [[appendix]]. Ira also saw the [[pancreas]], which makes insulin, and the huge [[aorta]]. The teacher said the digestive [[tract]] runs from the mouth to the [[anus]]. On Wednesday, Ira watched [[triage]] in the hospital's emergency room. A man with a broken leg had surgery under [[anesthesia]]. Later, a nurse showed Ira how to put in a [[catheter]]. After the long day, Ira felt a sharp [[spasm]] in her back. Still, she called Anna happily: "Today I signed up to be an [[organ]] donor!"
